reformulation: Agent-produced exact singleton elimination, committed in the run dir as output/reformulated.mps (NAME test15sp) from input/model.mps (NAME test15): delete x1..x32, the unique singleton columns of rows c1..c32; turn those 32 equalities into packing rows (E->L, RHS 1); keep all 44,211 retained matrix coefficients; substitute every retained cost as c_j - sum of the singleton costs in its support; carry the constant 315640009/62500 (=5050.240144) on one added fixed continuous column objconst (bounds [1,1]); source 4,516 integer vars / 32 rows / 44,243 nonzeros -> target 4,485 vars (4,484 BV + 1 fixed) / 32 rows / 44,211 nonzeros. The claim set is the complete integer and LP affine bijection in both directions, preserving the 4,484 retained coordinates and the exact objective, with all removed bounds and all original rows proved (cases/test15/preparation.json claims field).
claim_class: Exact bijective reformulation with retained-coordinate projection: 4 claims = {integer, LP} x {source->target, target->source}. Each claim carries a full coordinate sweep (one lower and one upper bound obligation per output variable, integrality facts in the two integer claims), one obligation per output row, one exact objective-identity Eq, a 4,484-pair retained-coordinate projection, and a complete inverse composition (4,485 resp. 4,516 residual Eqs). Reverse claims reconstruct each eliminated singleton as 1 - sum(retained y in its row). Obligation counts by claim: 22,487 / 22,550 / 18,003 / 18,034 = 81,074 total (cases/test15/preparation.json counts.obligations_by_claim).
claims: Forward integer claim (prepare_test15.py:31-46, integer=True, back=False): for each of the 4,485 target coordinates 'VarLower' and 'VarUpper' obligations resolved as bare 'Exact' or one-key refs, 4,484 'Int' facts, 32 row obligations, the objective residual, 4,484 projection entries and 4,485 inverse-composition residuals; 22,487 obligations (18,003 in the LP twin).

Reverse integer claim (back=True): 4,516 coordinate bounds, 4,484 'Int' facts, 32 'RowUpper' facts citing the source equality, and 32 packed 'Le' facts proving the target packing row from the source row plus retained nonnegativity (prepare_test15.py:48-56); 22,550 obligations; the LP twin has 18,034.

Eliminated coordinate definition: x_i = 1 - sum of the retained columns of row c_i, with 44,211 terms in total over the 32 rows (max 2,567 terms for x20, whose row c20 has 2,568 columns); the identical expression is emitted as the map entry, as a 'Le' step and (integer claim) as an 'Int' step.

Objective identity: d^T s + c^T y = 315640009/62500 + (c - A^T d)^T y, emitted as one terminal Eq whose terms are the 32 'RowEq' refs (forward, prepare_test15.py:57-59) or the fixed objconst column (reverse); the fixed column's [1,1] box is stated once as an EqPair premise (prepare_test15.py:34).

Projection and inverse: 4,484 literal [source_coord,target_coord] pairs per claim plus a complete inverse composition whose residual Eqs are dispatched by rule (identity, 'RowEq' combination, or the fixed column) (prepare_test15.py:60-66).
proof_encoding: RPA 2 text: 'RPA 2\n' + one compact JSON object {claims:[4 claim specs], blocks:[4 blocks]}, one block per claim in the same order (prepare_test15.py:73); 6,120,715 B, assembled to a 5,799,694 B RPX.

Block shape {steps:[{Lin:{id,kind,constant,terms}}], end:{Return:{map:[expression], checks:[ref]}}}; steps are built first and referenced by integer id from later steps and from the checks list (prepare_test54.py:20-32, prepare_test88.py Builder).

map = the whole coordinate map of that claim's direction: 4,484 literal identity entries of one term each (164,798-169,385 B per block) plus 32 row-wide reconstruction sums (520,462 B per reverse block).

checks is heterogeneous: bare 'Exact' strings (35,940 of the 81,074 obligations, of which 4,484 per claim are projection placeholders), one-key refs {'VarLower':j}/{'VarUpper':j}/{'Int':j}/{'RowEq':r}/{'RowUpper':r}, Lin step ids, and 32-66 'Local' ids.

Dense steps dominate the two reverse blocks: 32 'Le' steps with 44,211 'VarLower' terms (1,051,885 B resp. 1,051,881 B) and 32 'Int' steps with 44,211 'VarInt' terms (1,007,707 B); largest single step 61,003 B / 2,567 terms; kernel counters: obligations 81,074, linear_terms 398,159, substitution_terms 477,982, work 2,996,538, peak_live_facts 67, branches 0, execute 613,325 us (cases/test15/preparation.json kernel_runs).
agent_manual_work: Parsed the 1,527,612-byte MPS twice with independent decoders - whitespace token parse and fixed-field slots [4:12],[14:22],[24:36],[39:47],[49:61] - and cross-agreed on every row, all 48,759 column entries, RHS, INTORG/INTEND membership and section sequence before trusting any coefficient.

Found the 32 singleton columns by scanning the full 44,243-term incidence, then checked the identity submatrix, distinctness of all 4,516 supports, and row-pair connectedness (496 of 496 row pairs co-occur) to rule out duplicate-column and block-decomposition hypotheses.

Ran exhaustive exact dominance searches in integer micro-units: 135,545 proper-subset-plus-singletons pairs, 3,909 disjoint-union pairs, all 4,484 singleton-partition comparisons - no strictly cheaper replacement; plus a determinant -2 minor (x51,x80,x155 on rows c5,c20,c13) and an explicit fractional point to reject dropping integrality.

Hand-wrote the reformulated MPS with its own fixed-field writer and a 6-decimal formatter, re-read it with an independent parser, and exercised 1 zero packing + 4,484 single-column packings + 256 seeded greedy packings + the fractional witness through exact feasibility/objective/round-trip checks.

Authored audit.json (646,551 B: 4,484 retained objective changes, 32 deleted-variable reconstruction records, 32 row changes, domains, search counts) and report.md; the kernel preparer later bound that audit only by sha256 (prepare_test15.py:74).
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test15.py is 94 lines with defs prepare and main; it imports parse_mps,row_ref from prepare_affine; expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,sha from prepare_test40; substitute from prepare_test57; Builder from prepare_test88; fact,box,exact from prepare_test54 (lines 5-9) - a 6-deep import chain totalling 1,073 lines.

Inline hand-rolled machinery: removed/added detection by name-set difference (lines 15-16), singleton incidence scan (17-19), definitions/byrow/reverse construction (20-29), the four-claim loop with its per-obligation dispatch ladder (31-46), row/objective/projection/inverse obligations (48-66), claim-spec and block assembly (67).

Rule helpers: fact(builder,kind,e,terms,constant,terminal) collapses to 'Exact' when the residual is trivially true and otherwise builds a Lin step; box() proves e<=0 from variable bounds and asserts the ceiling (prepare_test54.py:16-32); Builder accumulates steps and validates refs against the model (prepare_test88.py).
Exact expression algebra: expression/plus/mul/expr_json/substitute over {constant, {index: Fraction}} with zero coefficients dropped (prepare_test40.py:72-85), re-exported through prepare_test57.py.

main() writes proof.rpa and request.json (request.json is exactly json.dumps(claims)), then runs canonical x2, assemble, verify and four hand-mutated counterexample RPAs that must come back INVALID (lines 71-90).
friction: Obligations are per coordinate per claim, so a 31-variable net edit produces 81,074 obligations and a 6,120,715 B RPA (5.62x the 1,089,457 B source.mcm); there is no way to say that 4,453 of the 4,485 coordinates are unchanged.

The 32 elimination definitions are re-expanded five times across the two reverse claims (2 map arrays at 520,462 B, 2 'Le' steps at 1,051,885/1,051,881 B, 1 'Int' step at 1,007,707 B = 4,152,397 B, 67.8% of the RPA) because nothing can name a definition and reference it.

The edit is re-derived by name-set differencing (prepare_test15.py:15-16) although audit.json already holds per-record diffs (4,484 objective-change and 32 reconstruction records); the preparer can only hash it (prepare_test15.py:74), so the claim-to-target binding is asserted, not checked.

The rule for each obligation is chosen by a hand-written ladder that compares builder.refexpr(check) against a recomputed expression, and the helpers come from five sibling case scripts (prepare_test15.py:5-9,40-55).

The single failing tool call was the agent's own six-decimal formatter rejecting an exact seven-decimal value ('An incidental print formatter rejected the fractional witness objective because it has seven decimal places'); kernel-side the four deliberate mutations were correctly rejected as INVALID at obligation 13452/13454/17971 and 'missing obligation'.
